alice_support: Escalation from customer: console shows region=eu-west but their requests are consistently landing in us-west. High p99 latency and a few 500s. Customer says billing shows tokens attributed to us-west. They provided a sample request id: rq_0a1b2c3d and trace 7f9e.
marco_runtime: Can you paste the raw request headers and a trimmed serving log for rq_0a1b2c3d? Also what endpoint/route were they hitting?
alice_support: Route is /v1/generate (standard). Customer sent a curl like this: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <tok>" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}'`
alice_support: Attached serving snippet from customer logs (they removed PII):
```
[2026-04-22T15:23:54Z] instance=prod-gpu-7 host=us-west-2a route=/v1/generate req=rq_0a1b2c3d status=200 latency_ms=312 trace=7f9e headers={Host:api.redwood.com, X-Client-Region: eu-west, X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.45}
```
alice_support: And from console metrics at the same time the dashboard shows eu-west for their org.
jenna_obs: I pulled the org-level region mapping — console display is driven by the cached preferred_region in the org record (cache TTL 10m). Serving routing uses SmartRouter service. We need to check SmartRouter decision logs for rq_0a1b2c3d.
marco_runtime: On SmartRouter side, we had a fallback tweak last week: if a request carries X-Client-Region we treat it as a soft hint and allow fallback to local capacity if preferred region is unavailable. If a proxy upstream rewrites that header, we could mis-route. Asking infra: did we change header precedence in the edge last week?
deploy-bot: deploy finished: edge-proxy v2.14.3 rolled at 2026-04-21T03:12:00Z (changes: allow X-Region override for internal partners)
marco_runtime: That deploy stands out. If edge now honors X-Region override, and some clients/partners add X-Client-Region=eu-west but traffic actually flows through a us-west edge, SmartRouter might pick us-west as the serving site (local availability) while the console still shows the org's preferred_region=eu-west. That would explain the mismatch and cross-region latency.
alice_support: Customer also reported intermittent auth failures (signature mismatch) on some requests — could that be related?
marco_runtime: Yes. If the request is routed through a different region, and we validate signed JWTs with region-bound claims (aud/iss or region in header), a mismatch can cause auth errors. Need to look at the specific failed req ids; ask customer for one, but we can also search logs for auth error patterns around that time.
jenna_obs: I queried the SmartRouter decision log for trace 7f9e:
```
2026-04-22T15:23:54Z decision_id=d_91c2 client=org_664 pref_region=eu-west hint=X-Client-Region:eu-west edge=us-west-2a chosen=us-west-2a reason=local_capacity_fallback
```
jenna_obs: Also saw billing attribution log: billing attributed tokens to region=us-west because serving instance host metadata used in the billing pipeline is us-west-2a.
marco_runtime: Root cause hypothesis: edge-proxy change allowed X-Region overrides and SmartRouter's fallback logic prefers local capacity over preferred_region when hint present. If hints come from clients or partner proxies that are geographically inconsistent, we can end up serving in a different region while console and org metadata still show preferred_region=eu-west (console uses cached store). This causes latency/regression and auth/billing misalignment.
alice_support: Proposed immediate mitigations?
marco_runtime: Short-term: 1) Turn off honoring of X-Client-Region at edge globally (rollback flag) — prevents external hints from overriding routing. 2) Reconcile console cache TTL to surface recent serving changes faster (reduce from 10m -> 1m) so display matches reality quicker. 3) Backfill billing attribution for affected tokens (manual correction for org_664) if needed.
jenna_obs: I can toggle the edge flag to ignore X-Client-Region now and watch SmartRouter decisions. I'll also open an alert for any decision where chosen_region != org.preferred_region for >1% of traffic in a 5m window.
marco_runtime: After toggling flag we should run a controlled test: hit the endpoint from an EU client with X-Client-Region header and confirm it routes to eu region. Also validate signed JWT auth passes when routed to preferred region.
alice_support: I'll ask the customer for one more failing req id for the auth errors but will tell them we've identified a probable routing header issue and are rolling a quick mitigation.
jenna_obs: Follow-up: created ticket ENG-4567 to change edge header precedence and update SmartRouter fallback policy; assigned to @marco_runtime and @infra_ops. Also adding a post-incident note to the ops runbook.
marco_runtime: Thanks. Once the flag is rolled back, I'll propose a long-term fix: require signed region hints (JWT claim) for any client-driven region override, and make SmartRouter prefer explicit org pinned_region over soft hints unless capacity is exhausted and verified by cross-region cost policy.
alice_support: Customer updated: they've accepted mitigation and will test after we flip the flag. Will follow up here with final confirmation.
jenna_obs: Postmortem actions: (a) fix dashboard cache TTL; (b) add reconciliation job to detect billing attribution drift; (c) add observability dashboard for region decision variance.
alice_support: Adding closure note: customer confirmed reduced latency after edge flag rollback, no more auth errors reported. Marking this thread resolved pending ENG-4567 progress.
